clue.text: Meeting to debate university entrance being restricted by class

indicators.note: a thing restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A university admissions debate is held in a restricted group.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a public gathering place or assembly held for open discussion of issues.

clue.text: Grand Prix about slavishly following rules

parts.note: Formula One (written Formula I) is the top class of Grand Prix motor racing
c. is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A racing driver obsessively sticking to the regulations at a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: Formulaic means following a set pattern mechanically, without originality.

clue.text: Unfortunate individual not quite getting gag

indicators.note: not quite the whole thing, so one letter is missing

parts.note: a wretch is an unhappy or unfortunate person

explanation.surface: A poor soul fails to land a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' usually trims a final letter; here the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to make the throat movements of vomiting, the same as to heave.

clue.text: Little Miss Malone onto us about what's on her wheelbarrow

parts.note: Molly Malone of the Dublin song, shortened ('Little') to Moll
taken as written
c. is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Molly Malone climbing on to us with her barrow.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Irish song, Molly Malone wheels her barrow through Dublin crying 'cockles and mussels'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles and mussels, the shellfish Molly Malone sells from her barrow, are bivalve sea creatures of that phylum.

clue.text: Architectural row: a media centre in North-East

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed after 'row' is itself a colon

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, as something sits in a place

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for North-East

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: Reads like a heading: an architectural dispute involving a media centre in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation mark after 'row' is itself part of the wordplay, so don't skip over it; 'centre' picks the middle letter of media.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns, a structural feature of classical buildings.

clue.text: Split in criticism primarily over dénouement of novel

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over the other
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is taken
a dénouement is an unravelling, so these letters are untangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A split among critics over the ending of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dénouement' looks like 'last letter of'; it is an anagram signal, making LOVEN from NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloven is the old past participle of cleave, meaning divided in two, as in a cloven hoof.

clue.text: Long-term detainee gets discharge and he lords it

indicators.note: the first piece gets the second inside it

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence
pee is urine discharged

explanation.surface: A long-serving prisoner gets released and starts acting superior.
explanation.walkthrough: A life peer is a member of the UK House of Lords whose title is not passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer sits in the House of Lords, so he is literally a lord, playing on 'lord it'.

clue.text: Let on about alien's brief communication

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's film extraterrestrial; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone reveals a short message about an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for writing a short note.

clue.text: Upstart's rare visit arranged

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is'; the definition is the noun upstart

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A social climber's visit is rarely set up.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is a person newly risen in status who is seen as pushy, a social climber.

clue.text: Clear air whether Smith initially takes leave

indicators.note: taking leave means departing, so these letters go from the word

parts.note: W H Smith is a British high-street newsagent chain; 'initially' asks for its initials W and H

explanation.surface: Whether Smith first gets permission to go, the air will be clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is poetic for the clear upper sky, the pure air above the clouds.

clue.text: Quickly name Labour's last prime minister with no end of following

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
having no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name the last Labour prime minister quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle off a list is to recite or name things rapidly and fluently.

clue.text: Burn peat or charcoal nuggets

indicators.note: nuggets are small lumps taken from something, so a small piece of these words is wanted

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting fire to lumps of peat or charcoal.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set fire to it deliberately, a synonym of burn as a verb.

clue.text: What landlord may do, denied right to evict

indicators.note: denied something means going without it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a pub landlord may run a house, a public house

explanation.surface: A landlord, refused his rights, may be stopped from evicting a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the landlord of a pub manages the premises, and a pub is often called a 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhouse someone is to turn them out of their home, a rare synonym of evict.

clue.text: Fuss caused by mate continuing to swear

indicators.note: one piece continues after another, so they follow in sequence

parts.note: a mate is a pal, a friend
to aver is to swear or declare something firmly

explanation.surface: A friend keeps cursing and causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means tiresome fuss or bother, a synonym of commotion over little.

clue.text: Pacino's outstanding in 'Home of the German Shepherd'?

parts.note: Al Pacino is the American actor; Al's is his first name with the possessive
ace means excellent or outstanding

explanation.surface: Al Pacino is excellent in a film titled after a German dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The German Shepherd dog is also called an Alsatian in Britain, so its 'home' is the French region it is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is the French region bordering Germany that gave the Alsatian dog its British name.

clue.text: One who turns out yacht's propellers?

definitions.text: One who turns out yacht's propellers?

parts.words: One who turns out yacht's propellers?
parts.note: propellers looks like screws, but a yacht is driven by the wind in its canvas, made by a craftsman

explanation.surface: A maker of yacht propellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailmaker makes the sails which drive a yacht along, its true propellers.

clue.text: Abandon endless project one's on

indicators.note: with no end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a jetty projects out over the water
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone is giving up on a never-ending project they are working on.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison means to throw away or discard, a synonym of abandon as a verb.

clue.text: Moult no bird gets over could be proposed

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece gets placed over the other

parts.note: taken as written
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling
Ted Moult was a British farmer and TV personality

explanation.surface: A bird that won't shed its feathers is put forward for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Moult was a farmer known from British TV panel shows and double-glazing adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nominated is to be put forward as a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Relation worked in the East

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A relative who had a job in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of or from Asia, the countries lying in the East.

clue.text: Appalling lairy chav lacking a code of good behaviour

indicators.note: appalling suggests something messed up, so these letters are rearranged
lacking something means it is missing, so it is removed

parts.note: lairy is British slang for flashy and aggressive; a chav is a loutish youth

explanation.surface: An awful, loud young lout shows no manners at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes one A from LAIRYCHAV, leaving LIRYCHAV to rearrange. A chav is British slang for a brash working-class youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is the medieval knightly code of honour and courtesy, now any gallant conduct.

clue.text: Not what Cagney was to Lacey anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cagney and Lacey were partners, so Cagney was never Lacey's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cagney & Lacey was an American TV police drama about two female detectives who were equal partners.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is a follower or assistant, which Cagney, an equal partner, was not.

clue.text: Issue of Right infiltrating traditional power

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: steam is the old-fashioned power of locomotives and mills

explanation.surface: Political: the Right worming its way into the old established power.
explanation.definitionFit: To stream is to issue or flow out continuously, as a verb of pouring forth.

clue.text: The game's up — Rolling Stone covering bald patch!

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece encloses the other
rolling means tumbling about, so these letters are mixed
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A rock star's bald spot gives the game away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The game' is rugby union; 'up' reads it from the bottom in this down clue, and 'Rolling' signals the anagram of Stone that wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head, so a deliberate bare patch.

clue.text: One in seven miners showing signs of nasal irritation

definitions.meaning: Snow White's seven dwarfs worked in a mine; one of them has this name
describes someone with a tickly nose who keeps sniffling and ahchooing

explanation.surface: One dwarf of the seven shows hay fever symptoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneezy is one of the seven dwarfs, and the word also describes someone prone to sneezes.

clue.text: Turn up clutching jar for stewed fruit

indicators.note: clutching means holding around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to turn up is to come or arrive
a pot is a jar or container

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a jar of stewed fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A compote is a dessert of fruit cooked slowly in syrup.

clue.text: Net gain

definitions.meaning: to net is to capture, as with a fish
to gain is to obtain or get hold of something

explanation.surface: Net gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch means to trap in a net, and also to obtain or get, as in catching a train.

clue.text: Granny's enthusiastic for this stuff

parts.note: Nan is a familiar name for granny; the 's here stands for 'is'
keen means eager or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Grandma is keen on some material.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, and stuff is an old word for woven fabric.

clue.text: And here in Rome is a singular morality

parts.note: et is Latin for and, with 'in Rome' signalling Latin for both words
hic is Latin for here, the language of Rome

explanation.surface: A tourist in Rome finds a unique moral code.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a single moral principle, the singular of the plural noun ethics.

clue.text: Wine is all right after third of bottle

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer
the third of a word is its third letter

parts.note: okay means all right

explanation.surface: Wine is fine once a third of the bottle is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert wine from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: Tanks beginning drive back to capture revolutionary old military machine

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
capturing means holding inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to rebut is to drive back or repel an attack or argument
Che Guevara is the standard crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A battle scene: tanks begin repelling an advance and capture a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet was a medieval siege engine that hurled stones using a counterweight.

clue.text: Acting boisterously in 'Equus'?

definitions.meaning: Equus is Peter Shaffer's stage play about a boy and horses, so a play about horses

explanation.surface: A review of a rowdy theatre production of Equus.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseplay is rough, noisy fooling around, and Equus is literally a play about horses.

clue.text: Retrospective focusing on Gaudi — clearly a Spanish hero

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the letters are read backwards
focusing on a stretch of words narrows in on letters within them

explanation.surface: A retrospective exhibition of the architect Gaudi, plainly celebrating a Spanish hero.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was the eleventh-century Castilian warrior Rodrigo Díaz, Spain's national hero.
